name: AI for sports movement research
research_focus: AI for sports, especially gymnastics teaching and running. Core methods are 2D/3D whole-body human pose estimation, skeleton-based action understanding, action quality assessment, and actionable coaching feedback. Gymnastics work includes standard-versus-incorrect action videos, fine-grained steps and labels, and dataset construction. Running work includes 3D pose, gait analysis, and sports biomechanics.
relevant: Sports or whole-body human movement pose estimation, action quality assessment, error detection, coaching, or actionable feedback.
Sports or whole-body action datasets, especially fine-grained annotation, action steps, or correct-versus-incorrect examples.
Transferable new methods for 2D/3D whole-body pose, skeleton action recognition, video action understanding, gait, or sports biomechanics.
maybe: Dance, rehabilitation movement assessment, or general whole-body action recognition without a direct sports setting.
Skeleton-based general action understanding or video-language methods that can explain or coach human movement.
Human motion generation that may transfer to movement feedback but is not directly about assessment.
Human mesh recovery (SMPL/SMPL-X), multi-view or wearable/IMU-based motion capture, and other human-motion sensing or modeling methods transferable to sports data collection.
irrelevant: Computer vision unrelated to human movement, such as autonomous driving, face recognition, generic object detection, or non-movement medical images.
Pose estimation only for hands, faces, animals, cameras, or other non-whole-body subjects.
Pure theory, NLP, or LLM work without a substantive connection to visual human movement.
